text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

---Newly-appointed Conservative leader Per Stig Moeller seems certain to be confirmed as chairman by the party's autumn conference, despite revelations of a 30-year-old drunken-driving offence, according to a survey of top officials.

---Danish business is still not sufficiently prepared for the introduction of EMU - Europe's economic and monetary union - in some EU member states in 1999, writes former Danish EU budget commissioner Henning Christophersen. Denmark opted out of joining EMU in a 1993 referendum. Also on EU affairs, Christophersen said political will would be necessary if enlargement to the east was to come about soon.

---An opinion poll conducted after the latest drink-driving scandals involving the past and present leaders of Denmark's Conservative Party show voter support for the party has plunged to 11.3 percent of the electorate. This is the lowest level since 1979 and 2.2 percent lower than before the leadership crisis started.

---A Danish complaints commission has ruled that the foreign ministry broke EU rules when it hired a German architect as part of a project build a joint Nordic embassy in Berlin without putting the contract out to open tender in all EU countries. Danish architects plan to ask the European Commission to act on the case. BORSEN
---Denmark's small local banks say they will resist takeover bids by big national banks such as Unidanmark, which recently said it was interested in acquiring provincial banks.
